title: CWS blocker: no in-product prominent disclosure and consent for user data
description:
Chrome Web Store User Data FAQ #10: the developer 'must describe the types of user data to be collected and how they will be used, and obtain the user's consent to that collection and use... The prominent disclosure and consent must occur within the Product's user interface. Disclosures in the Chrome Web Store description or inline installation page do not satisfy this requirement.' FAQ #3 confirms local-only processing still requires disclosure; FAQ #2 confirms 'clipping or scraping content from a website that the user visits' counts as handling user data.

Verified gap: the first-run wizard WelcomeStep (entrypoints/options/components/wizard/steps/WelcomeStep.tsx) is informational marketing copy only ('Privacy-first', 'No telemetry') with no enumeration of the user data types handled and no affirmative consent action. Wizard advance is generic navigation, not consent. Nothing blocks translation when consent is absent.

Data types that must be disclosed in-product: page text, selected text, focused-input text, subtitle/caption text, the opened PDF (opt-in), API credentials, and locally recorded page hostnames (statistics, host tracking on by default).

Fix: add a dedicated consent step to the setup wizard that enumerates the data types and their destinations and requires an explicit affirmative action, persist the consent decision in settings, and enforce the gate at the background translation entry point so no text is sent before consent is recorded. Add tests.
close_reason: In-product disclosure + consent gate shipped: lib/privacyConsent.ts (DATA_DISCLOSURE_ITEMS, version 2026-09-25), first-run wizard ConsentStep, Options->Statistics PrivacyConsentCard, popup ConsentRequiredPanel, background consent-required gate, content-script hard stop. Live-verified in Chromium 140 with the built extension: fresh profile lands on the Privacy step, Accept is disabled until the checkbox is ticked, popup shows the disclosure, and on a real page the block banner appears with zero network requests; after accepting, the gate opens and the pipeline reaches the provider stage. 952/952 tests pass.

title: CWS blocker: PRIVACY.md makes three inaccurate claims

title: provider-pool-resilience: Fix & harden all 13 provider-pool / round-robin / failover findings from deep analysis
design: Fix two structural bugs: (1) OpenAICompatibleService.translate() swallows ApiError into {success:false} where ProviderPoolCoordinator.dispatchWithFailover expects a thrown error -> circuit-breaker + failover are dead code in production (stub tests masked it). Fix: re-throw ApiError on transport/auth/rate-limit; keep {success:false} for content/parse failures. (2) PoolCursor advances in [0,slots.length) but dispatch indexes the filtered healthy[] subset -> skewed distribution + same-slot repeats. Fix: cursor over healthy pool's own index space. Plus: response_format memory keyed by baseUrl+model (survives rebuild), rate-limiter acquire() deadline bounded by requestTimeoutMs, hot-path config dirty-tracking (skip rebuild+updateConfig+AES-decrypt when settings unchanged), page-path cache guard for partial back-fills, PoolExhaustedError non-null lastError, pool testConnection skips open slots, double-retry layering bounded.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: real OpenAICompatibleService 429 from slot1 opens breaker + fails over to slot2 (integration test, mocked fetch, not throwing stub). AC2: even round-robin distribution when a slot is open (no skew/repeats). AC3: response_format stays disabled across rebuild when baseUrl+model unchanged. AC4: all-slots-fail error is non-null + descriptive. AC5: page path never caches partial back-fill. AC6: repeated translate() without settings change skips rebuild/updateConfig/decrypt. AC7: pnpm lint clean, pnpm test --run green, wxt build succeeds. AC8: no regression in 107 prior pool tests.
close_reason: All 8 phases complete. 13 findings fixed, 1723 tests pass, 0 regressions. Multi-key circuit-breaker failover now works in production.

title: BUG: Popup uses legacy provider readiness, shows 'setup not successful' when pool is ready
description:
ROOT CAUSE of 'popup shows setup not successful'.

entrypoints/popup/App.tsx:886 calls getProviderReadiness(settings.provider) — the LEGACY single-provider readiness which gates canTranslate on provider.connectionStatus === 'success'. But the new ProvidersSection UI writes to settings.providers[] (the pool) and never sets connectionStatus on the legacy mirror. So a user who configures a working provider in the Providers tab has a healthy pool, yet the popup sees the stale legacy mirror (connectionStatus='unknown') and shows the amber 'Provider not ready / Set up provider' banner, hiding the translate button.

The pool-aware getPoolReadinessStatus() was already written for exactly this (commit e4276e2, lib/providerReadiness.ts:208-260) and returns canTranslate:true (reason:'pool-ready') when a dispatchable (provider,key) slot exists — no connection test required. The ProvidersSection.tsx:81 banner already uses it. The popup was never migrated.

FIX: Switch popup to getPoolReadinessStatus(settings) + getPoolRecoveryMessage(). Keep the legacy getProviderReadiness for the wizard's own legacy mirror if needed. Add a popup test asserting pool-ready → no recovery banner + translate button visible.

Note: Bug is purely cosmetic/gating — translation itself is dispatched by the coordinator from settings.providers (Bug A is the actual dispatch failure). But fixing this is required for the symptom to clear.

title: BUG: ProviderPoolCoordinator.rebuild() does not propagate config changes to preserved member services
description:
ROOT CAUSE of 'Test works but translate fails'.

services/providerPool.ts rebuild() (lines 148-163) preserves the OpenAICompatibleService member instance when a key's id is unchanged, and updates existing.slot — but NEVER calls member.service.updateConfig(slot.providerConfig). The member service keeps its own private this.config (constructed at services/openaiCompatible.ts:43) from first construction.

REPRO: User sets up a provider in ProvidersSection (writes settings.providers[]). Test button works (it builds a FRESH ProviderConfig from UI state and calls providerTester.testConnection directly, bypassing the coordinator). But actual page translation dispatches through the coordinator's STALE member service, sending requests with the old/wrong apiKey/baseUrl/model → fails (401/404/network) and circuit-breaker opens.

FIX: In rebuild(), when existing member is preserved, call member.service.updateConfig(slot.providerConfig) so the OpenAI service reconfigures itself (config + rate limiter maxRpm + resets responseFormatDisabled). Guard for services that don't implement updateConfig (the TranslationService interface doesn't require it — only OpenAICompatibleService has it). Consider widening the interface.

TEST GAP: services/__tests__/providerPool.test.ts:124-138 only tests instance preservation with IDENTICAL settings. Needs a test: rebuild twice with the SAME keyId but DIFFERENT config, assert the member service received the new config (via updateConfig being called, or via dispatch using new values).

title: Subtitle pipeline review risk: reword 'DRM-safe scraping' and de-brand the listing
description: Chrome Web Store Malicious and Prohibited Products §4/§5 (unauthorized access to content; enabling access to copyrighted media). A full audit of all 11 platform handlers found NO DRM circumvention, no decryption, no key/licence handling, no cookie or credential capture, and no paywall/login/geo bypass. However several quotable items invite a §4/§5 reading: (a) shipped UI copy literally reads 'Movie and show subtitles translated via DRM-safe scraping' (lib/subtitleSites.ts:70); (b) the Max path re-fetches CDN caption segments from page context 'with the page's own auth context' (inject/maxVttPerformanceCapture.ts:1-11, 686) and re-attaches the manifest's manifest-params token onto synthesised segment URLs (lib/maxMpdSubtitles.ts:773-798); (c) bulk segment walks up to 500 (services/background.ts:217) and 3000 (lib/maxMpdSubtitles.ts:41) segments; (d) <all_urls> MAIN-world patching of fetch/XHR/JSON.parse/MediaSource at document_start (entrypoints/inject.content/index.ts:33-37). Fix: reword the 'DRM-safe' copy to plain language (e.g. 'reads the caption text your player already receives'); keep Netflix/Disney+/HBO Max/Youku brand names out of the store listing and single-purpose field (also Listing Requirements §4 keyword-spam risk); state the entitlement boundary explicitly in the listing, privacy policy, and a README note: only caption text the user's own logged-in session already receives is read, no video or audio is touched, and playback is never altered. Prepare a reviewer-facing answer for these questions.
close_reason: 'DRM-safe scraping' removed from PRIVACY.md, docs/guide/privacy.html and the listing; replaced with a factual statement (reads caption data the player already loaded, never decrypts protected media, never requests a DRM licence, never touches video/audio streams). docs/store-listing.md now states a rule: never name a streaming brand in listing copy.

title: Narrow web_accessible_resources to the one page-context resource
description: Chrome Web Store Use of Permissions §1 (narrowest scope). Verified: wxt.config.ts:41-48 exposes assets/* and icon/* to <all_urls>. The only genuine page-context consumer is content/selectionBubble/chip.ts:12 (chrome.runtime.getURL('icon/128.png')). assets/* has zero page-context consumers: the pdf.worker is loaded only from the pdf-viewer extension page (entrypoints/pdf-viewer/lib/pdfLoader.ts:18-25) and the CSS bundles are <link>ed only by extension pages (options.html, pdf-viewer.html, popup.html). Fix: set resources to ['icon/128.png'] (matches can stay <all_urls> because the chip runs everywhere), or inline the chip mark as a data: URL and drop web_accessible_resources entirely.

title: Reduce total test cases ~20% and cut suite runtime
description: Baseline: 104 files / 936 tests / 140.5s wall. Goal: ~749 tests and lower wall time. Approach: collapse table-driven micro-tests, merge redundant setup-heavy tests, delete cross-file duplicate tests, remove vi.waitFor polling in favor of deterministic awaits.

DONE. 936 -> 656 tests (-29.9%, target -20%); wall time 117s (forks, 5 flaky failures) -> ~61s stable, 4 consecutive all-green runs. Coverage 78.81% -> 80.17% statements (floor 70%).

Approach:
- Merged ~280 micro-tests across 60 test files: it.each tables -> single it + loop; adjacent same-harness one-assertion tests folded with per-facet comments. No assertion dropped (expect() counts verified identical vs HEAD per file).
- Deleted 3 exact cross-file duplicates in AdvancedSection.settings.test.tsx (subsumed by advancedCards/PerformanceCard).
- Root-caused the load-sensitive flake: background.test.ts held fake timers in a 30s-timeout test, so a timeout leaked them and every later test (incl. beforeEach) awaited a never-firing setTimeout. Fixed by zeroing OpenAICompatibleService 5xx backoff file-wide (existing __setRetryBackoffForTest seam), a file-level afterEach vi.useRealTimers(), and replacing vi.waitFor polls with deterministic microtask flushes.
- vitest.setup.ts: global afterEach vi.useRealTimers() safety net so this class cannot recur.
- vitest.config.ts: pool 'threads' (was default forks). Per-file fork cost dominated: same suite 117s/5 failures -> 63s all-green.

Evidence: tsc clean; eslint 34 errors all pre-existing at HEAD (webTranslateLifecycle 32, entrypoints/content.ts 1, services/providerPool.ts 1). No production source touched.

title: Make repeated page-translation start reinitialize cleanly
description: startTranslation tears down observers and clears piece state but does not remove existing translations or original markers before re-extraction. A second start command therefore skips marked originals, can leave old spinners/translations in place, and rebuilds an empty or incomplete piece registry; changing target language then starting again can retain stale-language output.
design: Phase 2 TDD: create one idempotent content-session teardown used at the beginning of startTranslationUnlocked and by stopTranslationUnlocked. It bumps/cancels first, stops observers, unregisters the resume writer, removes document and registered-shadow translation artifacts, resets registries/counters, then permits fresh extraction. Stop additionally writes the frozen resume snapshot before clearing. Repeated-start tests assert old-language output and spinners are removed and the new session re-extracts all originals.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated start commands remove or deliberately reuse old translated DOM without losing piece tracking; no stale spinner remains; target-language/settings changes are reflected; rapid double-start and start-during-active-request tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented shared idempotent page-session teardown; repeated Start now removes stale output and resets state before re-extraction. Focused lifecycle/display tests and compile pass.

title: Honor cache and batch budgets in default streaming translation
description: Streaming is enabled by default but sends every viewport batch directly to translateStream without success/failure cache lookup, text deduplication, or maxTextGroupLengthPerRequest/maxTextLengthPerRequest/provider budget partitioning. This makes the cache effectively write-only before stream calls and can send up to 16 roughly 1000-character pieces in one provider request despite the default 4-piece/2000-character limits.
design: Phase 1 TDD: extract the cache lookup, negative-cache partition, text dedup, article partition, effective budget split, duplicate rehydration, usage accounting, and success-only cache write portions of handleTranslate into shared background helpers. Both handleTranslate and WEB_STREAM_PORT execute the same prepared batches; stream batches preserve per-piece callbacks and terminal failed/partial metadata. Stream request forwards skipFailureCache. Tests assert cache hits avoid fetch, negative cache avoids fetch, duplicate text is sent once, article groups remain separate, and every provider request respects effective count/character budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming performs the same cache and negative-cache partitioning, deduplication, article-context partitioning, and effective batch-budget enforcement as non-streaming while preserving incremental updates and correct usage accounting.
close_reason: Implemented with focused lifecycle, cancellation, shared streaming preparation, provider deadline, cache/dedup/budget, and usage regressions; Phase 1 review accepted.

title: Abort and deadline web streaming requests
description: The background WEB_STREAM_PORT handler has no onDisconnect cancellation, and OpenAICompatibleService.fetchStream accepts no caller signal. Its timeout is cleared as soon as headers arrive, so a stalled SSE body can hang indefinitely. Tie each port request to an AbortController, abort on disconnect/supersession, propagate the signal through provider-pool streaming without failover on cancellation, and enforce a body/idle deadline.
design: Phase 1 TDD: add optional AbortSignal to TranslationRequest and propagate it through OpenAICompatibleService.translateStream, fetchStream, and ProviderPoolCoordinator.translateStream. The WEB_STREAM_PORT handler owns one AbortController, aborts on port disconnect, guards every postMessage after disconnect, and treats AbortError/cancelled as terminal without failure-cache writes or pool failover. Keep the request timeout active across SSE consumption by racing each reader.read against an idle timer based on requestTimeoutMs, canceling the reader in finally. Add provider and port regressions for disconnect and headers-then-stall.
acceptance_criteria: Disconnecting the web stream port aborts the active fetch without provider failover; a stream that returns headers then stalls terminates within the configured deadline; no postMessage is attempted on a disconnected port; tests cover both paths.
close_reason: Implemented with focused lifecycle, cancellation, shared streaming preparation, provider deadline, cache/dedup/budget, and usage regressions; Phase 1 review accepted.

title: Prevent stopped web streams from issuing stale fallback requests
description: When stop/restart bumps the content session, disconnecting WEB_STREAM_PORT resolves streamTranslate as a failure; translatePieces then sends a non-streaming fallback before checking whether the request session is still current. Async settings/category waits can also resume after stop and insert stale placeholders or issue stale work. Add session guards after awaits and before placeholder creation/fallback dispatch so superseded work exits without DOM or API side effects.
design: Phase 1 TDD: add content integration seams/tests around translatePieces and streamTranslate. Capture requestSession before async work; after loadSettingsCached and category detection, before placeholders, before guarded fallback sendMessage, and before result application, exit when sessionRegistry.isCurrent(requestSession) is false. Represent stream termination as success, recoverable error, or cancellation so disconnect caused by session bump cannot fall back. Focused proof: lifecycle tests assert zero placeholders and zero fallback messages after Stop/restart.
acceptance_criteria: Stopping or restarting during settings load or streaming creates no placeholder after teardown, issues no fallback translate message, and stale request cleanup cannot corrupt the new session's request count. Add integration-level content lifecycle regressions.
close_reason: Implemented with focused lifecycle, cancellation, shared streaming preparation, provider deadline, cache/dedup/budget, and usage regressions; Phase 1 review accepted.

title: Background: abort in-flight subtitle segment fetches on cancel
description: stopSubtitleSession cancels translation loops but FETCH_MANIFEST_SUBTITLES segment fetching (fetchDashSegmentBodies / fetchProgressiveDashSegments / fetchWithTimeout) has no AbortSignal, so a cancelled session keeps downloading every remaining segment and can hold the service worker alive. Add a per-tab fetch AbortController set, thread the signal through the manifest handler and segment loops, and skip the coordinator's failure toast for an aborted fetch.

title: Max VTT capture: recover a segment whose fetch failed

title: Stop during YouTube ASR AI re-align does not cancel the run
description:
User report: on a YouTube watch page the auto AI re-align starts (mini-progress with Stop). Clicking Stop hides the bar but re-align keeps running — progress reappears on the next batch and the LLM keeps burning tokens; translation still proceeds afterwards.

Root causes:
1. content/subtitleCoordinator.ts showRealignProgressUi Stop handler only calls cancelBackgroundSubtitleSession(), which backgrounds as CANCEL_SUBTITLE_SESSION -> stopSubtitleSession(tabId), a translation-streaming-session cancel. The in-flight RESEGMENT_YOUTUBE_ASR request has no cancellation path.
2. The ASR_REALIGN_PROGRESS listener registered in applyYoutubeAsrPipeline stays attached, so the next progress message re-creates the mini-progress bar after Stop.
3. services/openaiCompatible.resegmentYoutubeAsr batch loop has no abort check and fetchCompletion has no caller signal, so every batch still runs.

Fix: per-tab AbortController for resegment in background (aborted by CANCEL_SUBTITLE_SESSION), signal threaded through providerPool -> openaiCompatible -> fetchWithRetry, and a content-side realign cancellation handle wired into cancelBackgroundSubtitleSession that removes the progress listener and stops the pipeline before translation.

title: DOM-tier overlay shows stale/wrong subtitles after backward seek (unsorted cue buffer breaks binary-search lookup)
description:
**Symptom:** With subtitle video sites using the DOM tier (Youku, HBO Max fallback, generic handler), after the video is seeked (esp. backward) the overlay intermittently shows the wrong/stale subtitle text — or nothing — at the seeked position.

**Root cause (evidence-verified):**
1. `inject/domCueSource.ts:59` — the MAIN-world rolling 200-cue buffer is reset ONLY on track switch, never on seek.
2. `inject/domCueSource.ts:154` — `seekedHandler` closes the open cue at `max(currentTime, start+0.1)`, leaving a sliver in the buffer.
3. After a backward seek, the next sampled cue has an earlier startTime than that sliver → buffer becomes non-monotonic.
4. `content/subtitleCoordinator.ts:1075` `mergeDomOriginalCues` wholesale-replaces the coordinator buffer with this payload; the rebuild path (`rebuildTranslatedCues` → `adaptCueTimings`) never sorts.
5. `content/subtitleOverlay.ts:340` `findActiveCue` is a binary search requiring a sorted array → wrong index or -1 on inverted arrays.

**Simulation:** node seek-sim on the post-backward-seek buffer shape: 29/31 lookups returned a stale pre-seek cue instead of the current one (sorted reference: 11/31). Small buffers can pass by luck → intermittent ("sometimes").

**Contributing:** `inject/domCueSource.ts:105` — if the seeked position shows the same caption text as before, `sampleCue` skips (text === lastText), no cue is emitted, and the overlay stays blank while native captions are hidden.

**Safe tiers (verified):** intercept full-file (YouTube/Youku ASS), Max manifest/VTT capture (`mergeCues` sorts at `inject/maxVttPerformanceCapture.ts:301`), TextTrack/MSE — all feed sorted absolute-time cues; display is driven by `video.currentTime`.

**Suggested fix direction:** reset the DOM rolling buffer on seek (mirror `resetMaxVttCaptureForSeek`) and/or sort by startTime in `mergeDomOriginalCues`/`startDomCueSource.emit`, plus close-then-remove the sliver or clear the open cue on seek; add a regression test in `content/__tests__/subtitleOverlay.test.ts` + `inject/__tests__` for backward-seek buffer shape.
design: Root fix: reset the MAIN-world DOM cue source on every video seek and immediately sample the caption at the new currentTime, rather than retaining a closed pre-seek cue. Also listen for the existing SUBTITLE_SEEK_RESET bridge event so the source re-seeds after the coordinator clears its isolated-world overlay. Keep translation maps cached. Add inject/__tests__/domCueSource.test.ts covering backward seek ordering, repeated-caption re-emission, and bridge reset. Avoid renderer fallback/refactoring.
notes: Implementation sequence: write failing DOM-source tests; run focused test to confirm failure; add minimal source reset/reseed behavior and cleanup; run focused tests, full test suite, compile, lint; close only after validation.
close_reason: Implemented DOM cue buffer reset/reseed on video seek and SUBTITLE_SEEK_RESET, including repeated-caption handling; regression tests, compile, lint, and full suite verified.

title: Subtitle Plus mode — opt-in full-track quality translation (freeze glossary, parallel translate, reveal on completion)
description:
Opt-in subtitle mode for full-file sources (YouTube timedtext, WeTV/Netflix/Disney+/Coursera/Udemy VTT, manifest concat): freeze one terminology set before translating any cue, translate chunks with bounded parallelism against that frozen set, and reveal nothing until the run completes.

Motivation: the progressive pipeline refines the rolling glossary per chunk in completion order, and the playback-priority queue can reorder chunks on seek, so different chunks see different name/term snapshots. There is no user control to trade first-cue latency for whole-track consistency.

Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-subtitle-plus-mode-design.md

Hard constraints:
- Default off; absent `subtitleTranslationMode` means 'progressive'.
- The progressive path must be byte-for-byte unaffected (storage keys, cache keys, message fields, prompt content) — proven by regression tests.
- Plus uses its own scoped film-glossary key + cache identity (mode is a cache-key dimension) so progressive's existing keys are untouched.
- Never silently claim Plus is active: ineligible source, prep failure, or run failure falls back to progressive with an explicit notice.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Full-file source + mode 'plus' → preflight freeze, parallel chunks (bounded by the existing semaphore), no per-chunk properNouns forward merge, single terminal commit.
2. No translated cue reaches the overlay before commit; site captions stay visible during preparation; native body is blanked only at commit.
3. Stop (existing mini-progress button) cancels the run and restores/keeps original captions.
4. Partial chunk failure → those cues keep source text, the rest commit, and a partial-result notice is shown.
5. Incremental sources (DOM/MSE/manifest deltas) ignore the mode and run progressive, with the control shown disabled and a reason.
6. Mode 'progressive' (or absent) → identical behavior and identical cache keys to today.

title: Mid-page translate start: scroll jump + out-of-order chunk display
description:
## Context
User is scrolled to the middle of a page and clicks Translate Page (Alt+A).

## What works
- Viewport-first dispatch: IntersectionObserver (200px margin) only fires for the content the user is looking at; nothing above the viewport is translated unless scrolled into view. Lookahead prefetch goes only below the fold (lib/lookaheadPrefetch.ts).
- Reading-strip priority sort (lib/readingStripPriority.ts) puts the section heading + top-of-fold pieces first when >4 visible.

## Issues found
1. No scroll-anchoring protection: spinner placeholders (1.4em each) and translation blocks are inserted per chunk with no overflow-anchor CSS or JS scroll compensation anywhere. On sites with overflow-anchor: none, or in 'above' position mode (insert before original), the user's reading position jumps as each chunk renders.
2. Out-of-order chunk display (non-streaming): services/background.ts splits batches into sub-batches with concurrency 3; entrypoints/content.ts applies response.results in completion order, not reading order. On dense pages the visible batch is uncapped, so paragraphs below the focal point can translate before the heading in front of the user.
3. Resume restore jump: restoreFromSnapshot (entrypoints/content.ts ~L972) applies cached translations to ALL pieces including above-viewport ones on a previously translated page — page grows above the user and scroll jumps.
4. Initial viewport flush has no cap (only lookahead is capped at 4) — dense viewports produce large spinner storms.

## Suggested fixes
- Sort response.results back into piece order before applying (or tag sub-batch index).
- Cap the initial visible batch; measure + restore window.scrollY (or first visible anchor) after each chunk injection.
- Filter restoreFromSnapshot to near-viewport pieces; defer above-viewport restore until scrolled into view.

comments.author: Trung Nguyen
comments.text:
Fixed all four issues:

1. Scroll jump: new content/chunkStability.ts — captureScrollAnchor/restoreScrollAnchor measure the bottom-most visible piece parent before each chunk injection and re-align via scrollBy(delta) on the next frame (no double compensation with native anchoring; skips when user scrolled or anchor hidden by translation-only swap). Wired around spinner insertions, result application, streaming deltas, same-lang skip sweep, and snapshot restore.

2. Out-of-order chunks: orderResultsByPieces reorders background results into workPieces (reading) order before applying.

3. Resume restore jump: restoreFromSnapshot now only injects near-viewport pieces (isPieceNearViewport); off-screen pieces stay untranslated and get filled by the viewport observer (cache hit) when scrolled to.

4. Uncapped initial batch: ViewportObserver caps dispatch at DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_PIECES=16 per flush and drains the remainder in later batch windows.

Validation: npx vitest run → 199 files / 556 tests pass; npx tsc --noEmit clean; eslint clean on changed files.

design:
# Scientific PDF Setup Guide Site (GitHub Pages + GHCR image)

## Problem

PDF Translate requires a local Docker bridge, but the only setup instructions
live inside the repo (`docs/scientific-pdf-setup.md`). A user who installed the
extension from the store and has not cloned the repo cannot see the guide, and
the only supported path requires cloning the repo and building the image from
source (several minutes, needs git + full source tree). The offline surfaces in
the extension (PDF viewer card, Options → Advanced → Scientific PDF, wizard
Install step) do not link to any guide.

Verified constraint: the repo is currently private, and on the GitHub Free plan
GitHub Pages requires a public repository (GitHub docs: "If the account that
owns the repository uses GitHub Free… the repository must be public"). GHCR
storage is free only for public packages ("GitHub Packages usage is free for
public packages"). Decision: make the repo public; both the Pages site and the
GHCR image are then free.

## Goal

- A public, nicely rendered setup guide at a deterministic URL:
  `https://nguyensitrung.github.io/AnyLLMTranslate/guide/`
- A prebuilt bridge image on GHCR so users without the repo can be running in
  ~1 minute (`docker compose up -d`, image pull, no build).
- A "view setup guide" link on every surface that reports PDF Translate as
  unavailable, plus the README.

## Design

### 1. Guide site — `docs/guide/index.html`

Static, hand-authored HTML with inline CSS/JS (no build tooling, no new deps).
Dark theme matching the extension, sticky table of contents, copy-to-clipboard
buttons on every command block (vanilla JS).

Sections:

1. What this is / why Docker is required
2. Prerequisites — Docker Desktop (macOS/Windows), Docker Engine + Compose
   plugin (Linux), with official install links
3. **Path A — Quick Start (pull prebuilt image):** copy-paste compose file
   (below) + `docker compose up -d` + health check. No git, no clone, no build.
4. **Path B — Build from source (developer):** `git clone` + repo root +
   `./scripts/scientific-pdf-docker.sh up`
5. Verify health — expected `GET /health` JSON
6. Connect in the extension — Options → Advanced → Scientific PDF → Set up…
   wizard walkthrough
7. Everyday commands — `start` / `down` / `status` / `logs`
8. Rebuild / update — when bridge code changes, `git pull` + rebuild; for the
   pull path, re-run `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`
9. Common problems — table ported from `docs/scientific-pdf-setup.md`
10. Privacy — full PDF + short-lived credentials go to `serverUrl` (default
    loopback only); link to `PRIVACY.md`
11. Links — bridge API doc, repo, extension store

Quick Start compose snippet (must mirror the env/volumes/ports of the repo
compose; `image` tag is `latest`):

```yaml
services:
  scientific-pdf-bridge:
    image: ghcr.io/nguyensitrung/anyllm-scientific-pdf-bridge:latest
    container_name: anyllm-scientific-pdf
    ports:
      - "17890:17890"
    environment:
      MOCK_TRANSLATE: "${MOCK_TRANSLATE:-0}"
      JOB_TTL_SECONDS: "${JOB_TTL_SECONDS:-3600}"
      SCIENTIFIC_PDF_DATA_DIR: /data
      HF_ENDPOINT: "${HF_ENDPOINT:-}"
      HF_HOME: /root/.cache/huggingface
    volumes:
      - scientific-pdf-data:/data
      - scientific-pdf-models:/root/.cache
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  scientific-pdf-data:
  scientific-pdf-models:
```

Only `docs/guide/` is published; `docs/superpowers/`, `docs/PUBLISHING.md`,
etc. stay off the site. `docs/scientific-pdf-setup.md` stays as the repo-local
mirror and is updated to match the guide.

### 2. GHCR image publishing — `.github/workflows/bridge-image.yml`

- Triggers: push to `main` with paths `services/scientific-pdf-bridge/**`
  (includes the bridge `Dockerfile`); `v*` tags; `workflow_dispatch`.
- `docker/login-action` with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (permissions: `packages: write`,
  `contents: read`). Public repo → package is public → free storage/bandwidth.
- `docker/build-push-action` (buildx) pushes
  `ghcr.io/nguyensitrung/anyllm-scientific-pdf-bridge` with tags `latest`,
  `sha-<7>`, and `v<tag>` when building from a tag.
- Platforms: `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64` (Apple Silicon). If the arm64 build
  fails (wheel availability), fall back to amd64-only — Docker Desktop emulates
  amd64 on M-series via Rosetta.
- Repo `docker-compose.scientific-pdf.yml` stays build-based for developers.

### 3. In-extension links

New constant in `lib/scientificPdf.ts`:

```ts
export const SCIENTIFIC_PDF_SETUP_GUIDE_URL =
  'https://nguyensitrung.github.io/AnyLLMTranslate/guide/';
```

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `entrypoints/pdf-viewer/components/BridgeSetupCard.tsx` | Add "Read the full setup guide" link below the steps; opens via `chrome.tabs.create` (pattern already used in the codebase) |
| `entrypoints/options/sections/AdvancedSection.tsx` (Scientific PDF card) | Add "Setup guide" link button beside "Set up…" — always visible |
| `entrypoints/options/components/ScientificPdfWizard.tsx` (Install step) | Replace the `docs/scientific-pdf-setup.md` code text with a real link to the guide; keep the "rebuild only when bridge code changes" note |
| `README.md` PDF section | Add the guide URL next to the repo-doc link |

### 4. One-time repo operations (manual, done by maintainer)

1. Repo Settings → change visibility to **public**.
2. Repo Settings → Pages → Source: **GitHub Actions** (deploy workflow uses
   `actions/deploy-pages`).
3. First GHCR push auto-creates the package; visibility defaults to public for
   a public repo. Nothing else required.

## Non-goals

- No change to the bridge application, wizard flow, or provider pool handling.
- No version-pinning UX for the image (stays `latest`; `sha-` tags exist for
  reproducibility).
- No i18n.
- No in-app "start Docker for me" capability.

## Validation

- `docs/guide/index.html` renders correctly in a browser; copy buttons copy the
  right command blocks; TOC anchors work.
- `pnpm compile` passes; `vitest run` passes for the touched suites
  (`BridgeSetupCard.test.tsx` updated to assert the guide link).
- Bridge image workflow: on merge, the workflow builds and pushes the image;
  `docker compose up -d` with the guide's snippet pulls it and `GET
  /health` returns `{"status":"ok",…}`.
- Pages workflow: on merge, the site is reachable at
  `https://nguyensitrung.github.io/AnyLLMTranslate/guide/` and the extension
  links resolve there.

title: Fix player chrome icon position on Coursera (stranded top-left instead of bottom-right above control bar)
description:
User report: on Coursera video pages the in-player subtitle control icon shows at the top-left of the video; it should sit bottom-right, aligned with the player's control panel.

Root causes in code:
1. content/playerChrome/mountFloating.ts reposition(): invalid video rect (<80px, dynamic player mounting) early-returns and leaves host at initial top:0;left:0 (viewport top-left).
2. Floating anchor is 48px BELOW the video bottom (outside the player), not above the control band per design spec 2026-07-31-player-subtitle-chrome-design.md §5.2.
3. No scroll/resize tracking: position:fixed host drifts from the video on scroll.
4. Native mount candidates are trusted blindly; Coursera adapter's loose [class*="video-controls"] selector can match player-root/top-bar nodes.

Fix: anchor floating chrome bottom-right INSIDE the video above the control band; off-screen (never 0,0) while geometry invalid; rAF-coalesced scroll/resize tracking; validate native mount node occupies the video's bottom band before using it (else floating).
close_reason: Floating chrome now anchors bottom-right INSIDE the video, 56px above the bottom edge (above the native control band) per design spec §5.2; invalid video geometry off-screens the host instead of stranding it at viewport top-left (0,0); scroll/resize tracking (rAF-coalesced) keeps the fixed host glued to the video; native mounts are now validated to occupy the player's bottom control band (isPlausibleControlBar) before use, else floating fallback. TDD: 4 new regression tests (mountFallback geometry/tracking, host guard, lifecycle native-decision). Evidence: playerChrome suite 25/25, full suite 513/513, tsc clean, eslint clean.

title: Youku: seeks null out intercept-path session — translated chunks dropped as stale

comments.author: trungnguyen
comments.text:
Root cause: handleVideoSeeked's in-range guard (subtitleCoordinator.ts:1056) only fired when state.activeSource === 'manifest'. The fetch-intercept path used by Youku never sets activeSource (leaves it null), so every Youku seek — initial resume skip, every WAITING->PLAYING buffer transition, scrubs — fell through to the reset block which nulls state.activeSubtitleSessionId. Subsequent SUBTITLE_CHUNK_TRANSLATED messages were then dropped as stale (chunkSessionId !== null).

Fix: generalised the in-range guard to also check state.interceptOriginalCues (populated by handleIntercepted after parsing the full .ass/VTT body). In-range seeks now short-circuit for both paths. Tests: content/__tests__/subtitleCoordinator.test.ts (3 new).

NOTE: the index.browser.min.js 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading Dialogue)' error in the original report is from ANOTHER extension (likely Immersive Translate) or Youku's own player also intercepting the .ass URL — NOT from this extension. Our ASS parser is regex-based and never throws.

title: Address remaining web translation review follow-ups
description:
Consolidated non-blocking follow-ups from the web translation implementation reviews:

1. Aside accounting may double-count a repeatedly re-extracted unchanged aside piece because asideRegionChars is updated before deduplication.
2. Initial Shadow DOM discovery can still traverse roots beneath non-whitelisted direct body children; decide whether shadow registration should be gated by the body whitelist.
3. Removal-only mutations under unmarked parents, orphaned artifacts after a marked original is detached, and narrow ownerOriginalFor misattribution need additional lifecycle coverage.
4. Consider sharing selector constants used by mutation watcher, translation display, and tests to prevent drift.
5. Dynamic deduplication may drop a marked host when an unmarked ancestor is pending in the same flush.
6. TranslationResult should carry exact provider-backfilled IDs; background currently infers backfill from partial + source-equal text, leaving a narrow false positive for genuine same-text translations in partial responses.
7. Web content does not consume retryAfter yet; stream error plumbing should expose it when a retry UX is added.
8. sectionTranslate still ignores failed/backfilled items, which can leave dangling spinners or apply source back-fill as translation.
9. destroyZombie should probably bump/abort the session and hide mini-progress/pause/error chrome; it currently cleans listeners and DOM but does not fully invalidate stale async writes.
10. Resume unload writer is registered only when initial extraction finds pieces; mutation-only pages rely on stop-time snapshot behavior.
11. stopTranslation writes a resume snapshot even when enableWebResume is false; confirm desired cache lifecycle or gate it.

title: Clean up web-resume unload listeners across translation sessions
description: registerResumeSnapshotWriter adds pagehide and beforeunload closures, but stop only resets a boolean and never removes those listeners. Every stop/start cycle adds two more callbacks, causing repeated snapshot hashing/messages/IndexedDB writes on later unloads.
design: Phase 3 TDD: replace resumeSnapshotWriterRegistered with a stored stable EventListener reference. registerResumeSnapshotWriter first unregisters any prior reference; unregisterResumeSnapshotWriter removes pagehide and beforeunload and clears the reference. Call unregister during start teardown, stop teardown, and content-script zombie cleanup. Tests spy on add/removeEventListener and snapshot dispatch to prove repeated start/stop leaves at most one pair and stale handlers do not write.
acceptance_criteria: At most one active resume snapshot writer exists, stop and zombie teardown remove it, repeated start/stop cycles do not multiply writes, and pagehide/beforeunload behavior is regression-tested.

title: YouTube ASR realign: deferred follow-ups from flow audit
description: Not addressed in the audit fixes (each needs a product decision or a riskier shared change): (1) AI resegment batches are hard-split at 120 units with no cross-batch context, so a sentence spanning a batch edge is cut and a mid-run batch failure discards all previously paid batches without saving; (2) long multi-batch realign relies on the pending sendMessage response to keep the MV3 worker alive (handleResegmentYoutubeAsr does not call ensureKeepaliveAlarm, and doing so naively could leave the alarm latched forever); (3) resegmentFromCues chunks overlong cues by whitespace only, so CJK/Thai cues are never split and the hanging-word tables never apply; (4) Settings pre-align always selects the first ASR track, which may not be the language the viewer actually plays; (5) the passive intercept path holds the timedtext response until realign+translate finish, so native captions stay blank for the whole run (design trade-off, revisit if users report it).

PDF Download feature (pdf-download_20260618): Uses pdf-lib + @pdf-lib/fontkit for PDF generation. fontBytes is optional in translatedPdfGenerator (falls back to Helvetica). Font cached in IndexedDB via idb-keyval with key 'pdf-font:noto-sans:v1'. translateAllPages processes pages sequentially with per-page error isolation. usePdfDownload hook orchestrates 3-stage pipeline: translate-all → font fetch → PDF generation → browser download via anchor click. Noto Sans TTF fetched from fonts.gstatic.com with streaming progress. vi.stubGlobal returns previous value, not the spy — create vi.fn() separately.

Background subtitle chunk retry uses shouldRetry: isRetryableTranslationError from lib/subtitleRetry.ts (was () => true, which retried 4xx twice). The provider pool THROWS rather than returning {success:false}: ApiError with statusCode for client errors, PoolExhaustedError (own lastError) when failover exhausts slots. extractTranslationErrorStatus() unwraps PoolExhaustedError.lastError structurally (no imports, keeps the lib dependency-free). Rule: retry 408/429/5xx and status-less failures; fail fast on other 4xx. Note lib/translationErrors.ts isTransientTranslationError is for the NEGATIVE CACHE and deliberately treats auth/quota as transient — do not reuse it for retry decisions.

Subtitle platform handlers are registered in TWO worlds and must match. MAIN world (entrypoints/inject.content) hooks network traffic and stamps payloads with handler.platform; isolated world (entrypoints/content) resolves that id via getHandlerByPlatform() and transforms the body. Netflix+Disney+ were MAIN-only, so their intercepted subtitles resolved to null and passed through untranslated. Fix: single source of truth inject/subtitleHandlers/worldHandlers.ts (createPlatformHandlerSet / createIsolatedWorldHandlers), both entrypoints consume it, tests/unit/worldHandlers.test.ts asserts identical ordered platform-id lists and that every id resolves. Order is load-bearing: first-match-wins in detectCurrentHandler(), GenericSubtitleHandler LAST.

MSE subtitle tier (Tier 3) receives ONE SUBTITLE_MSE_CUES payload per SourceBuffer appendBuffer call (inject/mseInterceptor.ts) with no append/full/seq flag — each payload is a delta. The coordinator must accumulate: mergeMseOriginalCues() merges by start|end|text identity into state.mseOriginalCues (capped to the last MAX_MANIFEST_CUES, same bound as the manifest rolling buffer), rebuildMseTranslatedCues() applies state.mseTranslationMap, then translateMseCueTexts() sends only new texts (mirrors the DOM/manifest delta machinery). handleMseCues previously early-returned when activeSource==='mse', which froze the overlay after the first segment. Buffers are cleared in preemptLowerTierOverlay, resetCueBuffersForTrackSwitch, the seek reset (keeping the translation map as a text-keyed cache), and resetCoordinatorState.
